name: Nucleon pairing and neutron-star superfluidity
summary: The BCS gap equation with nuclear instead of phonon attraction gives 1S0 neutron superfluidity in the inner crust and 3P2 neutron and 1S0 proton pairing in the core; pair-breaking-formation neutrino emission just below Tc explains the rapid cooling of the Cas A neutron star.
sources: Baym, Pethick & Pines (1969). "Superfluidity in Neutron Stars". *Nature* 224, 673. [doi:10.1038/224673a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/224673a0)

Page et al. (2011). "Rapid Cooling of the Neutron Star in Cassiopeia A Triggered by Neutron Superfluidity in Dense Matter". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 081101. [arXiv:1011.6142](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.6142)

name: Vortex pinning and creep: flux lines vs pulsar glitches
summary: Pulsar glitches are modelled as catastrophic unpinning of quantized neutron-superfluid vortices from the crust lattice, the physics of Abrikosov flux-line pinning and Anderson-Kim thermally activated flux creep in type-II superconductors; post-glitch relaxation is vortex creep.
map: \oint\mathbf v_s\cdot d\mathbf l=h/2m_n\ (\text{neutron vortex})\leftrightarrow\Phi_0=h/2e\ (\text{flux line});\ \text{Magnus}\leftrightarrow\text{Lorentz force}
breaks: Neutron vortices are neutral and feel Magnus rather than Lorentz forces; pinning sites are nuclei of a Coulomb lattice, not material defects, and entrainment couples the superfluid to the crust.
sources: Anderson & Itoh (1975). "Pulsar glitches and restlessness as a hard superfluidity phenomenon". *Nature* 256, 25. [doi:10.1038/256025a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/256025a0)
Andersson et al. (2012). "Pulsar Glitches: The Crust is not Enough". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 109, 241103. [arXiv:1207.0633](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0633)

name: Degenerate Fermi gas: metals and white dwarfs
summary: The same degenerate Fermi-Dirac electron gas gives the Sommerfeld model of metals and the pressure that supports white dwarfs; Fowler applied Fermi statistics to white dwarfs in 1926, before Sommerfeld applied it to metals, and relativistic kinematics turns P~n^{5/3} into P~n^{4/3}, giving the Chandrasekhar mass.
sources: Fowler (1926). "On Dense Matter". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 87, 114. [doi:10.1093/mnras/87.2.114](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/87.2.114)
Chandrasekhar (1931). "The Maximum Mass of Ideal White Dwarfs". *Astrophys. J.* 74, 81. [doi:10.1086/143324](https://doi.org/10.1086/143324)

name: Band theory of neutrons in the neutron-star crust
summary: Bragg scattering of unbound superfluid neutrons by the nuclear lattice of the inner crust is computed with Bloch's theorem and band-structure methods; the resulting large neutron effective mass (entrainment) reduces the mobile superfluid fraction and challenges crust-only glitch models.
map: \psi_{nk}(\mathbf r+\mathbf R)=e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\psi_{nk}(\mathbf r):\ \text{electrons}\to\text{free neutrons};\ m_n^*/m_n\gg1\ (\text{entrainment})
sources: Chamel (2013). "Crustal Entrainment and Pulsar Glitches". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 110, 011101. [arXiv:1210.8177](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8177)
Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Coulomb crystallization of white-dwarf cores
summary: Carbon-oxygen ions in a cooling white dwarf freeze into a bcc Coulomb (one-component-plasma) crystal near Gamma~175; Gaia's cooling-sequence pile-up confirmed latent-heat release and phase separation, and the same bcc Coulomb lattice makes up neutron-star crusts.
sources: Van Horn (1968). "Crystallization of White Dwarfs". *Astrophys. J.* 151, 227. [doi:10.1086/149432](https://doi.org/10.1086/149432)

Tremblay et al. (2019). "Core crystallization and pile-up in the cooling sequence of evolving white dwarfs". *Nature* 565, 202. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x)

name: Debye cooling of crystallized white dwarfs
summary: Once a white-dwarf core crystallizes, its ionic heat capacity follows the Debye phonon law and falls as T^3 below Theta_D, so the oldest white dwarfs cool faster ('Debye cooling'), which shapes the faint end of the luminosity function used for cosmochronology.
sources: Tremblay et al. (2019). "Core crystallization and pile-up in the cooling sequence of evolving white dwarfs". *Nature* 565, 202. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x)

name: Crustal shear modes as magnetar QPOs
summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations in magnetar giant-flare tails (tens of Hz) are interpreted as global torsional modes of the crystalline crust, i.e. long-wavelength transverse acoustic phonons of the Coulomb lattice whose speed is set by the shear modulus mu~0.12 n_i Z^2 e^2/a.
sources: Strohmayer & Watts (2005). "Discovery of Fast X-Ray Oscillations during the 1998 Giant Flare from SGR 1900+14". *Astrophys. J.* 632, L111. [arXiv:astro-ph/0508206](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0508206)

name: Electron transport in white-dwarf and neutron-star matter
summary: Thermal and electrical conductivities of degenerate stellar matter are computed with the Boltzmann/Ziman theory of metals (electron-phonon Umklapp and electron-impurity scattering, Wiedemann-Franz); crust-cooling curves of accreting neutron stars imply a low-impurity, ordered rather than amorphous crust.
sources: Potekhin et al. (1999). "Transport properties of degenerate electrons in neutron star envelopes and white dwarf cores". *Astron. Astrophys.* 346, 345. [arXiv:astro-ph/9903127](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9903127)
Brown & Cumming (2009). "Mapping Crustal Heating with the Cooling Light Curves of Quasi-Persistent Transients". *Astrophys. J.* 698, 1020. [arXiv:0901.3115](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3115)

name: Wigner crystals and stellar Coulomb crystals
summary: Electron Wigner crystals in moire TMD superlattices and the ion crystals of white dwarfs and neutron-star crusts are both one-component plasmas that crystallize in a uniform neutralizing background once Coulomb energy beats kinetic energy (large r_s or large Gamma).
breaks: Stellar ions melt classically through thermal fluctuations, while 2D electron Wigner crystals melt quantum mechanically; moire Wigner crystals are pinned to an imposed superlattice and are two-dimensional.
sources: Regan et al. (2020). "Mott and generalized Wigner crystal states in WSe2/WS2 moiré superlattices". *Nature* 579, 359. [arXiv:1910.09047](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.09047)

name: Nuclear pasta as a liquid crystal
summary: In the neutron-star mantle, competition between nuclear surface tension and long-range Coulomb repulsion produces rod, slab and bubble 'pasta' phases with the symmetries of columnar and smectic liquid crystals (and of block-copolymer microphases); their elasticity is described with liquid-crystal theory.
breaks: Pasta is ordered by nuclear plus Coulomb forces at ~1e14 g/cm^3 with no solvent or thermal softness; its elastic constants are MeV-scale and the phases sit in a degenerate electron sea.
sources: Pethick & Potekhin (1998). "Liquid crystals in the mantles of neutron stars". *Phys. Lett. B* 427, 7. [arXiv:astro-ph/9803154](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9803154)
Caplan & Horowitz (2017). "Colloquium: Astromaterial science and nuclear pasta". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 041002. [arXiv:1606.03646](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03646)

name: Metallic hydrogen in giant planets
summary: Metallic hydrogen, predicted by Wigner and Huntington and proposed by Ashcroft as a high-Tc phonon superconductor (the idea behind hydride superconductors), makes up most of Jupiter's and Saturn's interiors, where its conductivity powers their dynamos; shock and static compression of the insulator-metal transition serve both fields.
sources: Wigner & Huntington (1935). "On the Possibility of a Metallic Modification of Hydrogen". *J. Chem. Phys.* 3, 764. [doi:10.1063/1.1749590](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1749590)
Ashcroft (1968). "Metallic Hydrogen: A High-Temperature Superconductor?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 21, 1748. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.21.1748](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.21.1748)
Celliers et al. (2018). "Insulator-metal transition in dense fluid deuterium". *Science* 361, 677. [doi:10.1126/science.aat0970](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0970)

name: Ab initio equations of state for giant-planet interiors
summary: DFT-based molecular dynamics provides the hydrogen-helium equation of state and the H-He immiscibility ('helium rain') used in Jupiter and Saturn interior models fitted to Juno and Cassini gravity data; DFT exchange-correlation and band-gap errors directly shift the predicted metallization boundary.
sources: Morales et al. (2009). "Phase separation in hydrogen-helium mixtures at Mbar pressures". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 106, 1324. [doi:10.1073/pnas.0812581106](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0812581106)

name: Superionic water ice in ice-giant interiors
summary: Superionic water, an oxygen crystal through which protons diffuse like a liquid, was predicted by ab initio simulation for Uranus and Neptune and identified in laser-shock experiments by nanosecond X-ray diffraction (fcc ice XVIII); it may explain the ice giants' non-dipolar magnetic fields.
sources: Cavazzoni et al. (1999). "Superionic and Metallic States of Water and Ammonia at Giant Planet Conditions". *Science* 283, 44. [doi:10.1126/science.283.5398.44](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.283.5398.44)
Millot et al. (2019). "Nanosecond X-ray diffraction of shock-compressed superionic water ice". *Nature* 569, 251. [doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1114-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1114-6)

name: Dust aggregation: from colloids to planetesimals
summary: The first stage of planet formation is aggregation of micron dust grains by Brownian motion and differential drift into fractal aggregates, followed by compaction, bouncing and fragmentation: the cluster-cluster aggregation and contact mechanics studied in colloids and granular matter.
map: D=\frac{k_BT}{6\pi\eta a}\to t_s=\frac{\rho_sa}{\rho_gv_{th}}\ (\text{Epstein});\ N\propto R^{d_f},\ d_f\approx1.8\text{-}2
sources: Blum & Wurm (2008). "The Growth Mechanisms of Macroscopic Bodies in Protoplanetary Disks". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 46, 21. [doi:10.1146/annurev.astro.46.060407.145152](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.astro.46.060407.145152)

name: Rubble-pile asteroids as granular bodies
summary: Most km-sized asteroids (Itokawa, Ryugu, Bennu) are gravitationally bound granular aggregates whose shapes, spin limits, regolith segregation and response to spacecraft contact are governed by granular rheology, friction and weak cohesion.
sources: Walsh (2018). "Rubble Pile Asteroids". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 56, 593. [doi:10.1146/annurev-astro-081817-052013](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-astro-081817-052013)

name: Amorphous ices and silicates in disks and dust
summary: Interstellar and protoplanetary grains are largely amorphous: vapour-deposited amorphous solid water and glassy silicates whose crystallization (annealing near the star) and glass-transition kinetics record thermal history and control volatile trapping at snow lines.

name: Fullerenes and PAHs: carbon nanostructures in space
summary: C60 was discovered in laser-vaporization experiments built to mimic carbon-star chemistry, opening the fullerene-nanotube-graphene family of carbon materials; fullerenes were later found in planetary nebulae and C60+ identified as a diffuse-interstellar-band carrier.
sources: Kroto et al. (1985). "C60: Buckminsterfullerene". *Nature* 318, 162. [doi:10.1038/318162a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/318162a0)
Cami et al. (2010). "Detection of C60 and C70 in a Young Planetary Nebula". *Science* 329, 1180. [doi:10.1126/science.1192035](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1192035)
Campbell et al. (2015). "Laboratory confirmation of C60+ as the carrier of two diffuse interstellar bands". *Nature* 523, 322. [doi:10.1038/nature14566](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14566)

name: Superconducting detectors for the CMB: TES and MKIDs
summary: CMB experiments (BICEP/Keck, SPT, ACT, Simons Observatory, CMB-S4) use arrays of transition-edge-sensor bolometers biased on the steep R(T) of a superconducting transition, and kinetic-inductance detectors that sense photon pair breaking through the Cooper-pair kinetic inductance.
sources: Irwin (1995). "An application of electrothermal feedback for high resolution cryogenic particle detection". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 66, 1998. [doi:10.1063/1.113674](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.113674)
Day et al. (2003). "A broadband superconducting detector suitable for use in large arrays". *Nature* 425, 817. [doi:10.1038/nature02037](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02037)

name: SQUID multiplexed readout of detector arrays
summary: Kilo- to hundred-thousand-pixel TES arrays for CMB polarimetry are read out with SQUID amplifiers in time-division or microwave (rf-SQUID resonator) multiplexing, exploiting the flux-periodic Josephson response and its low noise.

name: Superconducting phonon sensors and targets for dark matter
summary: Cryogenic dark-matter searches (SuperCDMS, CRESST) read athermal phonons from keV nuclear recoils with tungsten transition-edge sensors; superconductors themselves are proposed as targets for keV-mass dark matter because the gap 2Delta~meV sets an ultra-low threshold.
sources: Hochberg, Zhao & Zurek (2016). "Superconducting Detectors for Superlight Dark Matter". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 011301. [arXiv:1504.07237](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.07237)

name: Josephson parametric amplifiers in axion haloscopes
summary: Axion haloscopes (ADMX, HAYSTAC) detect axion-to-photon conversion in a microwave cavity with Josephson parametric amplifiers operating near the standard quantum limit, and HAYSTAC's squeezed-vacuum readout beats it.
sources: Du et al. (2018). "Search for Invisible Axion Dark Matter with the Axion Dark Matter Experiment". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 151301. [arXiv:1804.05750](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.05750)
Backes et al. (2021). "A quantum enhanced search for dark matter axions". *Nature* 590, 238. [arXiv:2008.01853](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01853)

name: Semiconductor targets for dark-matter electron recoils
summary: Silicon and germanium crystals are dark-matter targets: ionization-plus-phonon detectors for nuclear recoils, and single-electron skipper CCDs (SENSEI, DAMIC-M) whose ~1 eV band gap lets sub-GeV dark matter register through electron excitations across the gap.
sources: Essig, Mardon & Volansky (2012). "Direct Detection of Sub-GeV Dark Matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 85, 076007. [arXiv:1108.5383](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.5383)

SENSEI Collaboration (2025). "First Direct-Detection Results on Sub-GeV Dark Matter Using the SENSEI Detector at SNOLAB". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 134, 011804. [arXiv:2312.13342](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13342)

name: DFT and dielectric response for dark-matter scattering
summary: Dark-matter-electron scattering rates in crystals are computed from DFT crystal form factors and, with screening included, from the energy-loss function Im[-1/eps(q,omega)], so electronic-structure codes directly set direct-detection sensitivities.
sources: Essig et al. (2016). "Direct Detection of sub-GeV Dark Matter with Semiconductor Targets". *J. High Energy Phys.* 05, 046. [arXiv:1509.01598](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01598)
Knapen, Kozaczuk & Lin (2021). "Dark matter-electron scattering in dielectrics". *Phys. Rev. D* 104, 015031. [arXiv:2101.08275](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.08275)

name: Single-phonon excitations for sub-MeV dark matter
summary: Below ~MeV the dark matter's momentum transfer is below the inverse lattice spacing, so it scatters by creating single acoustic or optical phonons rather than nuclear recoils; polar crystals (GaAs, sapphire) with dark-photon-coupled optical phonons are proposed targets read out by phonon sensors.
sources: Knapen et al. (2018). "Detection of Light Dark Matter With Optical Phonons in Polar Materials". *Phys. Lett. B* 785, 386. [arXiv:1712.06598](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06598)

name: Dirac materials as light dark-matter targets
summary: 3D Dirac and Weyl semimetals with meV-scale gaps and weak in-medium screening have been proposed as targets for sub-MeV dark matter scattering or absorption on electrons, with directional sensitivity from anisotropic Dirac cones.
map: H_W=\hbar v_F\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k,\ E_g\to\text{meV};\ v_F\ll c\ \text{matches DM kinematics}
sources: Hochberg et al. (2018). "Detection of sub-MeV dark matter with three-dimensional Dirac materials". *Phys. Rev. D* 97, 015004. [arXiv:1708.08929](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08929)

name: Axion quasiparticles in magnetic topological insulators
summary: Magnetic topological insulators host a dynamical axion field theta(t) coupling as theta E.B; its quasiparticle (a longitudinal antiferromagnetic magnon mode) is proposed as a tunable meV-scale medium that converts axion dark matter into THz photons.
map: \mathcal L_\theta=\frac{\theta e^2}{2\pi h}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\leftrightarrow\mathcal L_a=g_{a\gamma\gamma}\,a\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B
breaks: The solid-state axion is an emergent collective mode with a material-set mass, not the QCD axion; only the electrodynamic coupling form is shared, and no candidate material is yet confirmed.
sources: Marsh et al. (2019). "Proposal to Detect Dark Matter using Axionic Topological Antiferromagnets". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 123, 121601. [arXiv:1807.08810](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.08810)

name: Kibble-Zurek defects: liquid crystals and the early universe
summary: Kibble's argument that causally disconnected regions choose independent vacua at a symmetry-breaking transition, leaving strings and monopoles whose overabundance inflation must dilute, was tested by quenching nematic liquid crystals and counting disclinations; Zurek's refinement gives defect density from the quench rate.
breaks: Nematic defects form in a dissipative, non-relativistic fluid with no gauge field and coarsen by friction; cosmic defects are relativistic, may be gauge strings, and evolve in an expanding spacetime.
sources: Kibble (1976). "Topology of cosmic domains and strings". *J. Phys. A* 9, 1387. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/9/8/029](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/9/8/029)
Zurek (1985). "Cosmological experiments in superfluid helium?". *Nature* 317, 505. [doi:10.1038/317505a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/317505a0)
Chuang et al. (1991). "Cosmology in the Laboratory: Defect Dynamics in Liquid Crystals". *Science* 251, 1336. [doi:10.1126/science.251.4999.1336](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.251.4999.1336)

name: Cosmic-string formation simulated in superfluid 3He
summary: Neutron-absorption hot spots in BCS-paired superfluid 3He re-cool through Tc and nucleate vortex tangles at the rate predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, a laboratory test of defect formation in early-universe phase transitions with a multicomponent order parameter.
breaks: 3He is a non-relativistic p-wave condensate whose vortices are global (no gauge field), whereas GUT strings are relativistic and typically local; the quench is spatially inhomogeneous, unlike a cosmological transition.
sources: Bäuerle et al. (1996). "Laboratory simulation of cosmic string formation in the early Universe using superfluid 3He". *Nature* 382, 332. [doi:10.1038/382332a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/382332a0)
Ruutu et al. (1996). "Vortex formation in neutron-irradiated superfluid 3He as an analogue of cosmic-string formation". *Nature* 382, 334. [doi:10.1038/382334a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/382334a0)

name: Skyrmions and cosmic textures
summary: Magnetic skyrmions and cosmological textures are both non-singular topological solitons of a sphere-valued order parameter classified by homotopy (pi_2 for 2D films, pi_3 for 3D cosmic textures); a collapsing texture was proposed to explain the CMB Cold Spot.
breaks: Skyrmions are static, DMI-stabilized and 2D; cosmic textures are 3D, unstable to collapse by Derrick's theorem and scale with the horizon. The Cold Spot texture interpretation is not established.
sources: Turok (1989). "Global texture as the origin of cosmic structure". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 63, 2625. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.2625](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.2625)
Cruz et al. (2007). "A Cosmic Microwave Background Feature Consistent with a Cosmic Texture". *Science* 318, 1612. [arXiv:0710.5737](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5737)

name: Emergent monopoles in spin ice and the monopole problem
summary: Spin-ice excitations behave as deconfined magnetic monopoles with a Coulomb interaction, a condensed-matter realization of the monopoles whose predicted overproduction at grand-unified transitions motivated inflation.
breaks: Spin-ice monopoles source the H field (div M), not B; they are emergent quasiparticles with non-quantized, material-set charge, unlike 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles of a broken gauge group.
sources: Castelnovo, Moessner & Sondhi (2008). "Magnetic monopoles in spin ice". *Nature* 451, 42. [arXiv:0710.5515](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5515)

name: Cosmic rays and pair breaking in superconducting devices
summary: Cosmic-ray muons and environmental gamma rays deposit energy in substrates as athermal phonons that break Cooper pairs, causing correlated quasiparticle bursts and error avalanches in superconducting qubits; this is the pair-breaking channel that cryogenic detectors use to see particles.
sources: McEwen et al. (2022). "Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits". *Nat. Phys.* 18, 107. [arXiv:2104.05219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05219)
Vepsäläinen et al. (2020). "Impact of ionizing radiation on superconducting qubit coherence". *Nature* 584, 551. [arXiv:2001.09190](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.09190)

name: DFT molecular dynamics for warm dense matter
summary: Equations of state, conductivities and opacities of warm dense matter (solid density, eV temperatures, partially degenerate) are computed with finite-temperature Kohn-Sham DFT molecular dynamics borrowed from electronic-structure theory, with Mermin's finite-T functional and temperature-dependent exchange-correlation.

name: Yukawa plasma crystals and colloidal crystals
summary: Charged dust grains in a plasma and charged colloids in an electrolyte both interact by a screened-Coulomb (Yukawa/DLVO) potential, crystallize when the coupling parameter is large, and let melting, defects and phonons be watched particle by particle.
breaks: Dusty plasmas are underdamped, strongly driven and open (charging currents, ion wakes), while colloids are overdamped by the solvent and in thermal equilibrium.
sources: Thomas et al. (1994). "Plasma Crystal: Coulomb Crystallization in a Dusty Plasma". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 73, 652. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652)

name: Plasmons, ion-acoustic waves and phonons in metals
summary: The bulk plasmon of a metal is the Langmuir wave of its electron gas, and longitudinal acoustic phonons in a metal are ion plasma oscillations screened by the electrons, exactly the ion-acoustic wave; Bohm and Staver used this to derive the sound speed of metals.
sources: Bohm & Staver (1951). "Application of Collective Treatment of Electron and Ion Vibrations to Theories of Conductivity and Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 84, 836. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.84.836](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.84.836)

name: Debye screening in plasmas and doped semiconductors
summary: Carriers in a non-degenerate semiconductor are a classical plasma: the extrinsic Debye length sets the width of space-charge regions and the screening of ionized donors, and in the degenerate (metallic) limit it becomes the Thomas-Fermi length, both from linearized Poisson-Boltzmann.

name: Boltzmann transport in solids and plasma kinetics
summary: Semiclassical electron transport in crystals solves the same kinetic equation as plasma physics, with a Lorentz-force streaming term and a collision integral (relaxation-time or Fokker-Planck); Landau damping of plasmons into the electron-hole continuum is the solid-state counterpart of collisionless Landau damping.
map:
\partial_tf+\mathbf v\cdot
abla_{\mathbf r}f+ rac{q}{\hbar}(\mathbf E+\mathbf v	imes\mathbf B)\cdot
abla_{\mathbf k}f=C[f],\ \mathbf v=\hbar^{-1}
abla_{\mathbf k}\epsilon_n(\mathbf k)
breaks: Solid-state carriers have band dispersions and Fermi-Dirac statistics with Pauli-blocked collisions and Umklapp; most plasma kinetic theory is classical, collisionless and long-range, with self-consistent Vlasov fields.

name: Two-dimensional plasmons in graphene and 2DEGs
summary: Electrons in graphene and semiconductor 2DEGs support gate-tunable 2D plasmons with omega~sqrt(q), imaged by infrared nano-imaging; drift-driven plasma-wave instabilities in field-effect transistors (Dyakonov-Shur) are the solid-state analogue of streaming instabilities and are used for THz detection.
sources: Chen et al. (2012). "Optical nano-imaging of gate-tunable graphene plasmons". *Nature* 487, 77. [doi:10.1038/nature11254](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature11254)

Dyakonov & Shur (1993). "Shallow water analogy for a ballistic field effect transistor: New mechanism of plasma wave generation by dc current". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 2465. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.2465](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.2465)

name: Dirac fluid: graphene's electron-hole plasma
summary: Near charge neutrality, thermally excited electrons and holes in clean graphene form a strongly interacting two-component relativistic plasma whose hydrodynamic transport violates the Wiedemann-Franz law by more than an order of magnitude.
sources: Crossno et al. (2016). "Observation of the Dirac fluid and the breakdown of the Wiedemann-Franz law in graphene". *Science* 351, 1058. [doi:10.1126/science.aad0343](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aad0343)

name: Dense hydrogen: superconductors and laser-shock experiments
summary: The insulator-metal transition of dense hydrogen and deuterium, the root of the metallic-hydrogen and hydride-superconductor programme, is probed both in diamond-anvil cells and in dynamic compression at NIF and the Z machine; the two disagree on the transition pressure, partly because of temperature and DFT functional choices.
sources: Knudson et al. (2015). "Direct observation of an abrupt insulator-to-metal transition in dense liquid deuterium". *Science* 348, 1455. [doi:10.1126/science.aaa7471](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa7471)
Celliers et al. (2018). "Insulator-metal transition in dense fluid deuterium". *Science* 361, 677. [doi:10.1126/science.aat0970](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0970)

name: X-ray diffraction and Thomson scattering of shocked matter
summary: Crystallography and inelastic scattering move into high-energy-density physics: nanosecond X-ray diffraction identifies crystal structures in laser-shocked samples, and X-ray Thomson scattering measures the dynamic structure factor S(k,omega), the same quantity inelastic X-ray and neutron scattering measure in solids, to infer temperature and ionization.
map: \frac{d^2\sigma}{d\Omega d\omega}=\sigma_T\frac{k_1}{k_0}S(\mathbf k,\omega),\ \mathbf k=\mathbf k_1-\mathbf k_0\ (\text{Bragg: }\mathbf k=\mathbf G)
sources: Glenzer & Redmer (2009). "X-ray Thomson scattering in high energy density plasmas". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1625. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.81.1625](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.81.1625)
Millot et al. (2019). "Nanosecond X-ray diffraction of shock-compressed superionic water ice". *Nature* 569, 251. [doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1114-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1114-6)

name: Quantum Monte Carlo for the warm dense electron gas
summary: Quantum Monte Carlo for the uniform electron gas, which underpins LDA exchange-correlation in condensed matter, was extended to finite temperature (path-integral and configuration PIMC) to give the warm-dense-matter exchange-correlation free energy, fighting the same fermion sign problem.
sources: Ceperley & Alder (1980). "Ground State of the Electron Gas by a Stochastic Method". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 45, 566. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.566](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.566)
Dornheim, Groth & Bonitz (2018). "The uniform electron gas at warm dense matter conditions". *Phys. Rep.* 744, 1. [arXiv:1801.05783](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.05783)

name: Exciton Mott transition by plasma screening
summary: At high photoexcitation density, screening by free carriers in 2D semiconductors shortens the screening length below the exciton radius, so excitons ionize into an electron-hole plasma with giant band-gap renormalization; this is the Mott criterion for pressure ionization in dense plasmas.
sources: Chernikov et al. (2015). "Population inversion and giant bandgap renormalization in atomically thin WS2 layers". *Nat. Photonics* 9, 466. [doi:10.1038/nphoton.2015.104](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphoton.2015.104)

name: Photon mass: plasma cutoff and Meissner effect
summary: Transverse light in a plasma obeys omega^2=omega_p^2+c^2k^2, as if photons had mass hbar*omega_p/c^2; Anderson used this plasma analogy to show that in a superconductor the Goldstone mode is absorbed and the photon becomes massive, giving London penetration depth lambda_L=c/omega_p(n_s), the step that became the Higgs mechanism.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)

name: Frozen-in flux vs Meissner flux expulsion
summary: An ideal-MHD plasma is a perfect conductor in which magnetic flux is frozen into the fluid, whereas a superconductor is more than a perfect conductor: London's equation actively expels flux; the contrast is the standard way to show the Meissner effect is thermodynamic, not just zero resistance.
map: \partial_t\mathbf B=\nabla\times(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)\ (\eta\to0,\ \dot{\mathbf B}=0\text{ in a static perfect conductor})\ \text{vs}\ \nabla\times\mathbf J_s=-\frac{n_se^2}{m}\mathbf B\Rightarrow\mathbf B=0
breaks: Ideal MHD has no condensate or gap and keeps whatever flux it started with; a superconductor reaches a unique equilibrium with B=0 inside, set by a macroscopic phase.

name: Guiding-centre drift and the Hall effect
summary: In crossed E and B fields charged particles drift at E x B / B^2 regardless of charge or mass; in a 2D electron gas this drift gives the classical Hall conductivity, and quantized cyclotron orbits (Landau levels) with skipping orbits at edges become the chiral edge states of the quantum Hall effect.

name: Helicons and Alfven waves in metals
summary: Compensated or uncompensated metals in a strong magnetic field are solid-state plasmas: they carry low-frequency helicon (whistler) waves, observed in sodium, and Alfven waves in bismuth, with dispersion set by carrier density and B exactly as in magnetized plasmas.

name: Non-reciprocal forces in complex plasmas and active matter
summary: Ion wakes downstream of levitated dust grains make grain-grain forces non-reciprocal, violating Newton's third law and breaking detailed balance; complex plasmas thus become a model system for the non-reciprocal and odd interactions central to active matter.
map: \mathbf F_{ij}\neq-\mathbf F_{ji}\Rightarrow\text{no Boltzmann distribution};\ T_i\neq T_j\ \text{for distinct species}
sources: Ivlev et al. (2015). "Statistical Mechanics where Newton's Third Law is Broken". *Phys. Rev. X* 5, 011035. [arXiv:1411.3982](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.3982)

name: Band topology of magnetized plasma waves
summary: Chern numbers and bulk-boundary correspondence, developed for electronic bands, classify the wave bands of magnetized cold plasmas; a topological gaseous plasmon polariton is predicted at plasma interfaces with a sign change of B or density.
map: C_n=\frac1{2\pi}\int\Omega_n(\mathbf k)d^2k\ \text{for the Maxwell-fluid eigenproblem }\omega\psi=H(\mathbf k)\psi
sources: Parker et al. (2020). "Topological Gaseous Plasmon Polariton in Realistic Plasma". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 195001. [arXiv:1911.02148](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02148)

name: REBCO high-temperature superconductors for compact tokamaks
summary: Rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) cuprate tapes carry high currents at 20 K and above 20 T, allowing compact high-field tokamaks (SPARC, ARC) because fusion power density scales as B^4 at fixed beta; quench protection and neutron degradation of the cuprate are open engineering problems.
sources: Creely et al. (2020). "Overview of the SPARC tokamak". *J. Plasma Phys.* 86, 865860502. [doi:10.1017/S0022377820001257](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022377820001257)

name: Nb3Sn and NbTi magnets for tokamaks
summary: The toroidal and poloidal field coils of ITER, JT-60SA, EAST and KSTAR are low-temperature type-II superconductors (Nb3Sn, NbTi) whose upper critical field, flux pinning and strain sensitivity set the achievable field and hence confinement.

name: Neutron damage and defects in fusion materials
summary: 14 MeV fusion neutrons create displacement cascades (vacancies, interstitials, transmutation helium) in tungsten and steel walls; point-defect and dislocation physics of crystals, measured in dpa, sets component lifetime.

name: Plasma etching and deposition in chip fabrication
summary: Reactive-ion etching, atomic-layer etching and plasma-enhanced CVD shape every semiconductor device; sheath-accelerated ions give anisotropic etches, and EUV lithography light comes from laser-produced tin plasmas.

name: Band theory behind semiconductor devices
summary: Bloch bands, effective masses, doping and carrier statistics from solid-state theory are the design language of transistors, LEDs and solar cells; device equations (drift-diffusion, Shockley diode, Shockley-Queisser) are band theory plus non-equilibrium carrier kinetics.

name: Synchrotron and XFEL light for crystallography
summary: Undulator synchrotron and free-electron-laser X-rays provide the brilliance for structure determination, resonant and inelastic scattering, and femtosecond diffraction of solids; Bragg's law and the structure factor are the analysis framework.
sources: Otwinowski & Minor (1997). "Processing of X-ray diffraction data collected in oscillation mode". *Methods Enzymol.* 276, 307. [doi:10.1016/s0076-6879(97)76066-x](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0076-6879(97)76066-x)

name: DFT shared by solid-state and quantum chemistry
summary: Kohn-Sham DFT is the workhorse of both communities; chemistry contributed hybrid and dispersion-corrected functionals (B3LYP, M06, DFT-D) while physics contributed plane-wave pseudopotential codes, and both test against wavefunction methods such as coupled cluster.
sources: Kohn & Sham (1965). "Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects". *Phys. Rev.* 140, A1133. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.140.A1133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.140.A1133)
Becke (1993). "Density-functional thermochemistry. III. The role of exact exchange". *J. Chem. Phys.* 98, 5648. [doi:10.1063/1.464913](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.464913)

name: Semiconductor physics and semiconductor devices
summary: Doped silicon, III-V and wide-gap semiconductors are one object seen twice: condensed matter supplies gaps, mobilities, recombination and junction physics; device physics turns them into MOSFETs, LEDs, lasers and photovoltaics.
sources: Bardeen & Brattain (1948). "The Transistor, A Semi-Conductor Triode". *Phys. Rev.* 74, 230. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.74.230](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.74.230)
Shockley & Queisser (1961). "Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells". *J. Appl. Phys.* 32, 510. [doi:10.1063/1.1736034](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1736034)

name: Soft-matter physics of biological materials
summary: Membranes, biopolymers, gels and cytoskeletal networks have energies of order k_BT, so entropic elasticity, fluctuations, self-assembly and viscoelasticity, the core of soft matter, set the mechanics of cells and biomolecules.
sources: de Gennes (1992). "Soft matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 64, 645. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645)

name: Proteins and nucleic acids as polymers
summary: Polymer physics (random walks, excluded volume, theta collapse, persistence length) gives the baseline for unfolded proteins and DNA; folding is a heteropolymer collapse with sequence-specific interactions.
sources: Flory (1949). "The Configuration of Real Polymer Chains". *J. Chem. Phys.* 17, 303. [doi:10.1063/1.1747243](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1747243)

name: Superconductors in accelerators
summary: Accelerators are the largest users of applied superconductivity: NbTi and Nb3Sn dipoles and quadrupoles bend and focus beams, and superconducting niobium RF cavities provide high-gradient, low-loss acceleration.

name: Device physics built on semiconductor physics
summary: Applied device physics (transistors, photovoltaics, sensors, thermoelectrics) rests on semiconductor band structure, doping and carrier transport.

name: Electronic side of thermoelectrics
summary: The thermoelectric figure of merit depends on the Seebeck coefficient and electrical conductivity from Boltzmann transport (Mott formula) and on the electronic thermal conductivity fixed by Wiedemann-Franz; band engineering optimizes the power factor S^2 sigma.

name: Phonon engineering for thermoelectrics
summary: High ZT needs low lattice thermal conductivity: strong anharmonicity, Umklapp and boundary scattering of phonons (as in SnSe and nanostructured bulk) suppress kappa_L without hurting electrons.
sources: Zhao et al. (2014). "Ultralow thermal conductivity and high thermoelectric figure of merit in SnSe crystals". *Nature* 508, 373. [doi:10.1038/nature13184](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13184)

name: Cells and tissues as active matter
summary: The actomyosin cortex and epithelial tissues are active gels and active nematics; topological defects in epithelial monolayers localize stress and trigger cell extrusion, the same +1/2 defect physics as in microtubule active nematics.
sources: Marchetti et al. (2013). "Hydrodynamics of soft active matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 85, 1143. [arXiv:1207.2929](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.2929)
Saw et al. (2017). "Topological defects in epithelia govern cell death and extrusion". *Nature* 544, 212. [doi:10.1038/nature21718](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature21718)

name: Chemical physics uses condensed-matter DFT
summary: Chemical physics borrows DFT and periodic electronic-structure methods for spectroscopy, reaction barriers and surface chemistry.

name: Flocking theory and collective animal behaviour
summary: Vicsek and Toner-Tu theories of polar active matter describe starling flocks, fish schools and bacterial swarms; field data showing starlings interact with a fixed number of topological neighbours fed back into active-matter models.
sources: Vicsek et al. (1995). "Novel Type of Phase Transition in a System of Self-Driven Particles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1226. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226)

Ballerini et al. (2008). "Interaction ruling animal collective behavior depends on topological rather than metric distance: Evidence from a field study". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 105, 1232. [arXiv:0709.1916](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1916)

name: Helfrich elasticity: from liquid crystals to membranes
summary: Lipid bilayers are two-dimensional smectic-A liquid crystals; Helfrich, co-inventor of the twisted-nematic display, transferred Frank curvature elasticity to membranes, giving the bending energy that predicts red-blood-cell shapes and vesicle fluctuations.
sources: Helfrich (1973). "Elastic Properties of Lipid Bilayers: Theory and Possible Experiments". *Z. Naturforsch. C* 28, 693. [doi:10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209](https://doi.org/10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209)

name: Worm-like chain elasticity of single DNA molecules
summary: Force-extension curves of single DNA molecules in optical and magnetic tweezers are fitted by the worm-like-chain model of semiflexible polymers, giving a 50 nm persistence length and confirming entropic elasticity at the single-molecule level.
sources: Bustamante et al. (1994). "Entropic elasticity of λ-phage DNA". *Science* 265, 1599. [doi:10.1126/science.8079175](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.8079175)

name: Flory-Huggins phase separation and biomolecular condensates
summary: Membraneless organelles (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) form by liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent proteins and RNA, described with Flory-Huggins polymer-solution theory and its sticker-spacer extensions.
sources: Brangwynne et al. (2009). "Germline P Granules Are Liquid Droplets That Localize by Controlled Dissolution/Condensation". *Science* 324, 1729. [doi:10.1126/science.1172046](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1172046)

Hyman, Weber & Jülicher (2014). "Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation in Biology". *Annu. Rev. Cell Dev. Biol.* 30, 39. [doi:10.1146/annurev-cellbio-100913-013325](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-cellbio-100913-013325)

name: Rugged energy landscapes: glasses and protein folding
summary: Random-energy and spin-glass landscape ideas developed for glass formers were applied to proteins, giving the folding funnel and the principle of minimal frustration: foldable sequences have a folding temperature well above their glass temperature.
sources: Bryngelson & Wolynes (1987). "Spin glasses and the statistical mechanics of protein folding". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 84, 7524. [doi:10.1073/pnas.84.21.7524](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.84.21.7524)

name: Jamming and unjamming of biological tissues
summary: Confluent epithelia undergo a rigidity (jamming) transition controlled by cell shape rather than density, analogous to athermal jamming; unjammed, fluid-like tissue is linked to wound healing, asthma and cancer invasion.
sources: Bi et al. (2015). "A density-independent rigidity transition in biological tissues". *Nat. Phys.* 11, 1074. [arXiv:1409.0593](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0593)

name: Brownian colloids as force probes
summary: Optical and magnetic tweezers are calibrated by the Brownian motion of a trapped colloidal bead: equipartition and the Lorentzian power spectrum with Stokes drag give the trap stiffness that turns position into force.

name: Granular friction and earthquake faults
summary: Fault gouge is a sheared granular layer: rate-and-state friction, stick-slip instability, dilatancy and shear localization measured on granular materials explain earthquake nucleation and aftershock behaviour.
sources: Marone (1998). "Laboratory-derived friction laws and their application to seismic faulting". *Annu. Rev. Earth Planet. Sci.* 26, 643. [doi:10.1146/annurev.earth.26.1.643](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.earth.26.1.643)

name: Crackling noise: Barkhausen jumps and earthquakes
summary: Barkhausen noise from domain-wall avalanches in ferromagnets and earthquakes on faults both show power-law size distributions explained by depinning of an elastic interface in a random medium, the 'crackling noise' universality family.
breaks: Fault systems have long-range elastic interactions, healing and inertia that can produce characteristic quakes; universality-class assignments and exponents differ, and magnetic avalanches are tuned by an external field rather than tectonic loading.
sources: Sethna, Dahmen & Myers (2001). "Crackling noise". *Nature* 410, 242. [arXiv:cond-mat/0102091](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0102091)

name: Rock magnetism and the paleomagnetic record
summary: Remanent magnetization of magnetite-bearing rocks, explained by Neel's theory of thermally activated single-domain grains, records the geomagnetic field; stripes of reversed magnetization on the sea floor confirmed sea-floor spreading and plate tectonics.
sources: Vine & Matthews (1963). "Magnetic Anomalies Over Oceanic Ridges". *Nature* 199, 947. [doi:10.1038/199947a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/199947a0)

name: Mantle and core mineral phases behind seismic structure
summary: The post-perovskite transition of MgSiO3, found by high-pressure X-ray diffraction and ab initio theory, explains the D'' seismic discontinuity above the core-mantle boundary, and hcp iron's elastic anisotropy explains inner-core seismic anisotropy.
sources: Murakami et al. (2004). "Post-Perovskite Phase Transition in MgSiO3". *Science* 304, 855. [doi:10.1126/science.1095932](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1095932)

Oganov & Ono (2004). "Theoretical and experimental evidence for a post-perovskite phase of MgSiO3 in Earth's D″ layer". *Nature* 430, 445. [doi:10.1038/nature02701](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02701)

name: Ab initio mineral physics of Earth's deep interior
summary: DFT elastic constants and melting curves of iron alloys and silicates at 100-360 GPa supply the seismic velocities, densities and core temperature that seismology alone cannot fix, at conditions difficult to reach in experiments.
sources: Oganov & Ono (2004). "Theoretical and experimental evidence for a post-perovskite phase of MgSiO3 in Earth's D″ layer". *Nature* 430, 445. [doi:10.1038/nature02701](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02701)

name: NV centres: point defects in a wide-gap semiconductor
summary: The nitrogen-vacancy centre is a deep point defect in diamond's 5.5 eV gap whose spin triplet ground state is optically initialized and read out at room temperature, making defect physics of semiconductors the basis of nanoscale quantum sensing.
map: H=DS_z^2+\gamma_e\mathbf B\cdot\mathbf S,\ D/h\approx2.87\,\text{GHz};\ \delta B\sim\frac{1}{\gamma C\sqrt{T_2t}}
sources: Doherty et al. (2013). "The nitrogen-vacancy colour centre in diamond". *Phys. Rep.* 528, 1. [arXiv:1302.3288](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3288)

name: SQUID magnetometry
summary: SQUIDs turn flux quantization and Josephson interference into femtotesla magnetometers used for magnetoencephalography, geophysics, rock magnetism and condensed-matter susceptibility measurements.
sources: Hämäläinen et al. (1993). "Magnetoencephalography—theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 65, 413. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.65.413](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.65.413)

name: NV magnetometry imaging of 2D magnets
summary: Scanning single-spin (NV) magnetometry images stray fields of atomically thin magnets such as CrI3 quantitatively, resolving layer-dependent magnetization and domains; it is now a standard probe of 2D magnetism and spin textures.
sources: Thiel et al. (2019). "Probing magnetism in 2D materials at the nanoscale with single-spin microscopy". *Science* 364, 973. [arXiv:1902.01406](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.01406)

name: Superconducting magnets for MRI
summary: Clinical MRI scanners use persistent-mode NbTi solenoids at 1.5-7 T; type-II superconductivity with strong flux pinning gives the stable, homogeneous field whose Larmor frequency sets image signal and resolution.

name: Spintronic memory and read heads in electronics
summary: Giant and tunnelling magnetoresistance moved from discovery to hard-disk read heads within a decade, and spin-transfer-torque MRAM is now embedded in CMOS logic processes as non-volatile memory.
sources: Baibich et al. (1988). "Giant Magnetoresistance of (001)Fe/(001)Cr Magnetic Superlattices". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 61, 2472. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2472](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2472)

name: Quantum-dot light emitters and photovoltaics
summary: Size-tuned colloidal and perovskite nanocrystals are used in displays (QLEDs), downconverters and solar cells; confinement sets the emission colour and multiple-exciton generation offers a route past the Shockley-Queisser limit.
sources: Murray, Norris & Bawendi (1993). "Synthesis and characterization of nearly monodisperse CdE (E = sulfur, selenium, tellurium) semiconductor nanocrystallites". *J. Am. Chem. Soc.* 115, 8706. [doi:10.1021/ja00072a025](https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00072a025)

name: Two-dimensional semiconductor channels for transistors
summary: Monolayer MoS2 and related TMDs provide atomically thin channels with sizeable gaps, immune to short-channel effects that limit silicon scaling; contact resistance and dielectric integration are the open device problems.
sources: Radisavljevic et al. (2011). "Single-layer MoS2 transistors". *Nat. Nanotechnol.* 6, 147. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2010.279](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2010.279)

name: Graphene nanopores for single-molecule sensing
summary: A single graphene layer is thinner than the spacing of DNA bases, so ionic current through a graphene nanopore resolves translocating molecules with sub-nanometre thickness, a step toward solid-state sequencing.
sources: Garaj et al. (2010). "Graphene as a subnanometre trans-electrode membrane". *Nature* 467, 190. [arXiv:1006.3518](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3518)

name: Phase-change glasses for non-volatile memory
summary: Chalcogenide glasses such as Ge2Sb2Te5 switch in nanoseconds between amorphous and crystalline states with very different resistivity and reflectivity; crystallization kinetics and glass stability are the device physics of phase-change memory.
sources: Wuttig & Yamada (2007). "Phase-change materials for rewriteable data storage". *Nat. Mater.* 6, 824. [doi:10.1038/nmat2009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmat2009)

name: d-band theory and descriptor-based catalyst design
summary: DFT calculations of adsorption energies on metal surfaces, organized by the position of the d-band centre and linear scaling relations, explain why gold is inert and drive computational screening of catalysts through volcano plots.
sources: Hammer & Nørskov (1995). "Why gold is the noblest of all the metals". *Nature* 376, 238. [doi:10.1038/376238a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/376238a0)

Zhao et al. (2019). "Theory-guided design of catalytic materials using scaling relationships and reactivity descriptors". *Nat. Rev. Mater.* 4, 792. [doi:10.1038/s41578-019-0152-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41578-019-0152-x)

name: STM imaging of the local density of states
summary: STM, developed in surface science, measures the sample's local density of states via tunnelling (Tersoff-Hamann); spectroscopic STM became a core probe of band structure, superconducting gaps, vortex cores and quasiparticle interference in quantum materials.
sources: Binnig et al. (1982). "Surface Studies by Scanning Tunneling Microscopy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 57. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.57](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.57)
Tersoff & Hamann (1985). "Theory of the scanning tunneling microscope". *Phys. Rev. B* 31, 805. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.31.805](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.31.805)

name: Surface crystallography and reconstruction
summary: Surfaces have their own 2D lattices and reciprocal lattices; low-energy electron diffraction and STM reveal reconstructions such as Si(111) 7x7, extending bulk diffraction theory to the 17 wallpaper groups.
sources: Binnig et al. (1983). "7 × 7 Reconstruction on Si(111) Resolved in Real Space". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 50, 120. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.120](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.120)

name: Raman and infrared spectroscopy of phonons
summary: Molecular vibrational spectroscopy carries over to crystals, where Raman and IR probe zone-centre optical phonons; in graphene the G and 2D Raman bands count layers, measure strain, doping and electron-phonon coupling.
sources: Ferrari et al. (2006). "Raman Spectrum of Graphene and Graphene Layers". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 97, 187401. [arXiv:cond-mat/0606284](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0606284)

name: Tight binding as periodic LCAO / Huckel theory
summary: The tight-binding band model is the molecular-orbital LCAO (Huckel) method applied to a periodic lattice: graphene's pi bands are the infinite-molecule limit of benzene's Huckel orbitals, and Slater-Koster parameters play the role of resonance integrals.
map: E(\mathbf k)=\epsilon_0+\sum_{\mathbf R}t(\mathbf R)e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\leftrightarrow\text{H\"uckel }E=\alpha+2\beta\cos\frac{2\pi j}{N}
sources: Slater & Koster (1954). "Simplified LCAO Method for the Periodic Potential Problem". *Phys. Rev.* 94, 1498. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.94.1498](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.94.1498)

name: DMRG, QMC and coupled cluster across fields
summary: DMRG, invented for 1D spin chains, became a leading method for strongly correlated molecules (active spaces of transition-metal clusters), while coupled cluster and quantum Monte Carlo moved from nuclear and quantum chemistry into solids; agreement across methods is the benchmark standard in both fields.
sources: Chan & Sharma (2011). "The Density Matrix Renormalization Group in Quantum Chemistry". *Annu. Rev. Phys. Chem.* 62, 465. [doi:10.1146/annurev-physchem-032210-103338](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-physchem-032210-103338)

name: Superionic conductors for solid-state batteries
summary: Solid electrolytes such as Li10GeP2S12 are superionic crystals in which a rigid anion framework hosts liquid-like Li-ion diffusion through connected sites; crystal structure and its percolating channels set ionic conductivity.
sources: Kamaya et al. (2011). "A lithium superionic conductor". *Nat. Mater.* 10, 682. [doi:10.1038/nmat3066](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmat3066)

name: High-throughput DFT for battery and energy materials
summary: Databases of DFT-computed formation energies, voltages and phase stability (Materials Project and successors), now accelerated by machine-learned potentials, screen cathodes, electrolytes and thermoelectrics before synthesis.
sources: Jain et al. (2013). "Commentary: The Materials Project: A materials genome approach to accelerating materials innovation". *APL Mater.* 1, 011002. [doi:10.1063/1.4812323](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4812323)

name: BCS surface resistance of SRF cavities
summary: Niobium superconducting RF cavities are limited by the BCS surface resistance from thermally excited quasiparticles, plus residual losses from trapped flux; nitrogen doping and Nb3Sn coatings are gap-engineering responses that raise Q0 and gradient.

name: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering of cuprates
summary: High-resolution RIXS at synchrotrons measures paramagnons and charge-density-wave correlations in cuprates; it revealed incommensurate charge order competing with superconductivity in YBCO.
sources: Ghiringhelli et al. (2012). "Long-Range Incommensurate Charge Fluctuations in (Y,Nd)Ba2Cu3O6+x". *Science* 337, 821. [arXiv:1207.0915](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0915)

name: Synchrotron ARPES of topological surface states
summary: Spin- and angle-resolved photoemission with tunable synchrotron light identified the odd number of spin-momentum-locked surface Dirac cones that define 3D topological insulators, and later Fermi arcs in Weyl semimetals.
sources: Hsieh et al. (2008). "A topological Dirac insulator in a quantum spin Hall phase". *Nature* 452, 970. [arXiv:0902.1356](https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.1356)

name: Topological origin of equatorial waves
summary: Applying Chern-number band topology to the rotating shallow-water equations shows that the equatorial Kelvin and Yanai waves are topologically protected edge modes forced by the sign change of the Coriolis parameter at the equator.
sources: Delplace, Marston & Venaille (2017). "Topological origin of equatorial waves". *Science* 358, 1075. [arXiv:1702.07583](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07583)

name: Polaron hopping and Marcus electron transfer
summary: Small-polaron hopping in solids (Holstein) and Marcus electron transfer in solution are the same theory: an electron moves between sites when vibrational (phonon) fluctuations bring the two diabatic energies into resonance, with reorganization energy equal to twice the polaron binding energy.
sources: Holstein (1959). "Studies of polaron motion: Part II. The 'small' polaron". *Ann. Phys.* 8, 343. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(59)90003-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(59)90003-X)

name: Landauer transport in nanoscale transistors
summary: As MOSFET channels shrink to a few nanometres, current is computed as transmission through modes (Landauer-Buttiker, non-equilibrium Green's functions) rather than drift-diffusion; the ballistic limit gives the conductance quantum per mode.
sources: Datta (2004). "Quantum Transport: Atom to Transistor". *Cambridge University Press*. [doi:10.1017/cbo9781139164313.012](https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139164313.012)

name: DFT as computational physics' largest application
summary: Kohn-Sham DFT with plane waves, pseudopotentials, FFTs and iterative eigensolvers is among the most heavily used computational methods in all of science; numerical analysis (basis convergence, k-point sampling, self-consistency mixing) controls its accuracy.
sources: Kresse & Furthmüller (1996). "Efficiency of ab-initio total energy calculations for metals and semiconductors using a plane-wave basis set". *Comput. Mater. Sci.* 6, 15. [doi:10.1016/0927-0256(96)00008-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0927-0256(96)00008-0)

name: Molecular dynamics of supercooled liquids and jamming
summary: Simulations of Lennard-Jones and soft-sphere mixtures supply dynamical heterogeneity, the Kauzmann and mode-coupling tests and jamming criticality, but are limited to ~microsecond times, about 10^-6 of the laboratory glass-transition timescale.
sources: Debenedetti & Stillinger (2001). "Supercooled liquids and the glass transition". *Nature* 410, 259. [doi:10.1038/35065704](https://doi.org/10.1038/35065704)

name: DMRG and tensor networks for correlated electrons
summary: DMRG, invented for quantum spin chains, is a variational method over matrix product states; PEPS, MERA and their 2D cylinder implementations now give benchmark ground states of Hubbard and frustrated spin models, limited by area-law entanglement growth.
sources: Schollwoeck (2011). "The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states". *Ann. Phys.* 326, 96. [arXiv:1008.3477](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3477)

name: Entanglement structure of correlated ground states
summary: Area-law entanglement in gapped correlated phases is what makes tensor-network compression possible; deviations (log corrections at criticality, topological entanglement entropy) diagnose the phase.

name: SQUIDs as instrumentation
summary: SQUIDs are the most sensitive magnetic-flux detectors and the readout amplifiers of cryogenic sensor arrays; their noise is set by Josephson-junction physics and can approach the quantum limit.

name: Kramers pairs protect topological insulators
summary: The antiunitary time-reversal operator with Theta^2=-1 forces Kramers degeneracy at time-reversal-invariant momenta, giving the Z2 invariant and protecting the surface Dirac cone against non-magnetic backscattering.
sources: Kane & Mele (2005). "Z2 Topological Order and the Quantum Spin Hall Effect". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 146802. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506581](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506581)

name: Josephson voltage standard and the 2019 SI
summary: The AC Josephson effect fixes voltage to frequency through K_J=2e/h exactly; with e and h fixed in the 2019 SI, Josephson arrays realize the volt and, with the Kibble balance, the kilogram.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

name: Quantum Hall resistance standard
summary: Hall plateaus at R_xy=h/(nu e^2) independent of material and geometry realize the ohm via the von Klitzing constant R_K=h/e^2, exact in the 2019 SI.
sources: von Klitzing, Dorda & Pepper (1980). "New Method for High-Accuracy Determination of the Fine-Structure Constant Based on Quantized Hall Resistance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 45, 494. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.494](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.494)

name: Bloch bands as an eigenvalue problem
summary: Band structure is the spectral decomposition of a lattice-translation-invariant Hamiltonian: Bloch's theorem block-diagonalizes it by crystal momentum, leaving finite Hermitian matrices H(k) to diagonalize.
map: [H,T_{\mathbf R}]=0\Rightarrow H=\bigoplus_{\mathbf k}H(\mathbf k),\ H(\mathbf k)u_{n\mathbf k}=E_n(\mathbf k)u_{n\mathbf k}

name: Spin-group symmetry classification of altermagnets
summary: Altermagnets are defined by spin-group symmetry, in which spin and lattice operations act independently when spin-orbit coupling is negligible; opposite-spin sublattices related by a rotation rather than a translation or inversion give d-, g- or i-wave spin splitting.
map: [C_2\|C_{4z}]\ \text{(spin flip }\otimes\text{ lattice rotation)}\Rightarrow E_\uparrow(\mathbf k)-E_\downarrow(\mathbf k)\propto k_xk_y
sources: Šmejkal, Sinova & Jungwirth (2022). "Emerging Research Landscape of Altermagnetism". *Phys. Rev. X* 12, 040501. [arXiv:2204.10844](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.10844)

name: Quantum Monte Carlo and the fermion sign problem
summary: Determinant, auxiliary-field and diagrammatic QMC map correlated electrons onto Monte Carlo sampling in imaginary time; for doped fermions and frustrated magnets the weights turn negative and the sign problem makes cost exponential.
sources: Troyer & Wiese (2005). "Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 170201. [arXiv:cond-mat/0408370](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0408370)

name: Superconductivity as broken U(1) gauge symmetry
summary: A superconductor is the condensed-matter Higgs phase: a charged condensate with a phase that breaks U(1), whose would-be Goldstone mode is eaten by the photon, giving the Meissner effect and flux quantization.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)

name: Ginzburg-Landau theory is the abelian Higgs model
summary: The Ginzburg-Landau free energy of a superconductor is, term by term, the static abelian Higgs Lagrangian; the coherence length and penetration depth are the inverse Higgs and photon masses, and kappa=lambda/xi separates type I from type II exactly where Nielsen-Olesen strings attract or repel.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)

name: Spin liquids: order without symmetry breaking
summary: Quantum spin liquids are the main counterexample to the Landau paradigm: frustration prevents spontaneous symmetry breaking down to T=0, and the low-energy theory instead has emergent gauge fields and fractionalized spinons, so the phase is classified by topology rather than an order parameter.
map: f=|\theta_{CW}|/T_N\gg1;\ \text{no local }\langle\mathbf S_i\rangle\neq0,\ \text{emergent }\mathbb Z_2\text{ or U(1) gauge field}
sources: Balents (2010). "Spin liquids in frustrated magnets". *Nature* 464, 199. [doi:10.1038/nature08917](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature08917)

name: Nematic order, Goldstone modes and homotopy of defects
summary: A nematic breaks rotational symmetry with order-parameter space RP^2; its director fluctuations are Goldstone modes and its defects are classified by homotopy groups, pi_1(RP^2)=Z_2 allowing half-integer disclinations, which is the general topological theory of defects in ordered media.
sources: Mermin (1979). "The topological theory of defects in ordered media". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 51, 591. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.51.591](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.51.591)

name: Magnons as Goldstone bosons and their counting
summary: Magnons are the Goldstone modes of broken spin-rotation symmetry: antiferromagnets have two linearly dispersing type-A modes, while ferromagnets have one quadratic type-B mode because the broken generators have a non-zero commutator expectation; Mermin-Wagner forbids such order in 2D at T>0.
sources: Watanabe & Murayama (2012). "Unified Description of Nambu-Goldstone Bosons without Lorentz Invariance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 251602. [arXiv:1203.0609](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0609)

Mermin & Wagner (1966). "Absence of Ferromagnetism or Antiferromagnetism in One- or Two-Dimensional Isotropic Heisenberg Models". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 17, 1133. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133)

name: Altermagnets break time reversal without magnetization
summary: Altermagnets lift Kramers spin degeneracy by breaking the combined time-reversal-plus-translation symmetry of ordinary antiferromagnets while keeping zero net moment, so T-odd responses (anomalous Hall, spin splitting) appear without stray fields.
sources: Krempaský et al. (2024). "Altermagnetic lifting of Kramers spin degeneracy". *Nature* 626, 517. [doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06907-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06907-7)

name: The tenfold way from T, C and chiral symmetry
summary: Gapped free-fermion phases fall into ten Altland-Zirnbauer classes set by whether time reversal T, particle-hole C and chiral S symmetries are present and square to +1 or -1; with dimension this gives the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors.
sources: Altland & Zirnbauer (1997). "Nonstandard symmetry classes in mesoscopic normal-superconducting hybrid structures". *Phys. Rev. B* 55, 1142. [arXiv:cond-mat/9602137](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9602137)
Kitaev (2009). "Periodic table for topological insulators and superconductors". *AIP Conf. Proc.* 1134, 22. [arXiv:0901.2686](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.2686)

name: Space groups and representations in crystals
summary: The 230 space groups and their irreducible representations label Bloch bands, phonon branches and selection rules, explain systematic absences in diffraction, and the crystallographic restriction (no 5-fold axes) made quasicrystals a surprise.
map: \{R|\mathbf t\}\psi_{n\mathbf k}=\psi_{n,R\mathbf k};\ \text{little group }G_{\mathbf k}\ \text{irreps label bands};\ 2\cos(2\pi/n)\in\mathbb Z
sources: Shechtman et al. (1984). "Metallic Phase with Long-Range Orientational Order and No Translational Symmetry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 53, 1951. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1951](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1951)

name: Topological quantum chemistry via band representations
summary: Induced (band) representations of space groups decide whether a set of bands can come from localized symmetric Wannier orbitals; when they cannot, the bands are topological, which turned representation theory into a high-throughput topology classifier.
sources: Bradlyn et al. (2017). "Topological quantum chemistry". *Nature* 547, 298. [arXiv:1703.02050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02050)

name: Berry curvature as the curvature of a bundle
summary: Berry connection and curvature are a U(1) connection and its curvature on the bundle of Bloch states over the Brillouin-zone torus; the Chern number is the first Chern class and the quantum geometric tensor combines a metric with this curvature.
map:
